rows.available: For a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic different from p, the absolute Galois group has p-cohomological dimension2, satisfies the finite-cohomology condition, and finite p-primary modules have the stated perfect local Tate pairings.
rows.needed: The absolute group of Q2 has cd2=2 and finite cohomology for finite2-primary modules, as needed in the local Iwasawa descent argument.
rows.argument: Use the local statement with p=2 and local field Q2. The global no-real-place hypothesis in5.1 is not being applied to Q: the local field may be realized as a split completion of an imaginary quadratic field, and the assertion depends only on its absolute local Galois group. The coefficient T chi is finite free over Z2 with continuous action; its finite quotients fit these local statements.
rows.limits: No assertion cd2(G_Q,S)=2 is made. The real global case remains governed by5.7.

rows.available: For an elliptic curve over a finite extension of Qp, the local points contain a finite-index subgroup isomorphic to the additive group of the ring of integers.
rows.needed: For each actual local quadratic twist, local elliptic torsion is finite and H0(Qq,V2(E) tensor chi)=0.
rows.argument: The displayed finite-index subgroup is torsion free, so the torsion subgroup injects into the finite quotient. The Galois-invariant subgroup of the Tate module is the inverse limit of the local rational2-power torsion groups under multiplication2, which is zero for a finite2-primary group. Any invariant vector in the rational Tate module becomes an invariant integral vector after multiplying by a fixed power of2. Hence it is zero. The quadratic character twist is the Tate module of the actual local quadratic elliptic twist, so the same argument applies.
rows.limits: No good-reduction or odd-residue-characteristic assumption is imposed; this includes Q2. No uniform order bound is claimed.

rows.available: Localized local duality identifies local cohomology of a finite-type coefficient complex with the appropriately shifted dual cohomology of its Tate dual. For a finite-dimensional Q2 representation V it gives H2(K,V) dual to H0(K,V dual(1)).
rows.needed: H2(Qq,V2(E) tensor chi)=0 for every fixed local quadratic type used for F2 and Fbad.
rows.argument: The elliptic Weil pairing identifies V2(E) with V2(E) dual(1). Since chi is quadratic, the twist has the same self-duality. Apply localized local duality to this finite-dimensional Q2 representation. The preceding local-torsion argument gives zero H0 of the dual twist, hence zero H2. This is local duality only; no global no-real-place hypothesis is imposed on Q.
rows.limits: The self-dual Weil pairing, quadratic nature of chi, and separate local-torsion input are retained. The Iwasawa descent identity and global localization comparison are not supplied by this statement.
